newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: ABN AMRO looks to U.S. for growth.
newsitem.headline: ABN AMRO looks to U.S. for growth.

text.p: ABN Amro Holding NV sees its recent listing in the U.S. as providing a chance to finance acquisitions in future, if such opportunities arise, ABN Amro chairman Jan Kalff said in a Swiss newspaper interview.
In Saturday's edition of Finanz and Wirtschaft, Kalff also said it was too early to make a prediction for the bank's results based on the first five months of 1997.
He said however the bank was targeting a growth in earnings of at least 10 percent on an annual basis, together with an increase in earnings per share of at least 7.5 percent.

ABN Amro most recently bought Standard Federal Bancorporation Inc, based in Troy, Michigan. It bought Chicago Corp last year, and also owns the Chicago-based LaSalle banking group, along with European American Bank based in New York State. It has 11 of its own branches in the U.S.
"We are still busy with the integration of Standard Federal," Kalff said in the interview.
"But if there is an opportunity, we will examine it. Large acquisitions in the U.S. will also be possible, because we are now directly present on the largest capital market in the world," he said.
ABN Amro completed a listing of American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) on Wednesday, May 21.
"The expansion will continue in the U.S.," Kalff said.

He added its U.S. banking activities were growing at a rate of 10 to 15 percent, and the rate could accelerate through further acquisitions. "America will therefore become more important for us," he said.

Asked whether ABN Amro would consider acquiring German-based BHF Bank, he said noted the bank was not represented throughout Germany, and also was not a retail bank. He said that in Europe at the moment, "there are no interesting banks to buy."
He added that he saw mergers between banks in various separate European countries as more likely than cross-border European mergers.
"I see big cross-border mergers or takeovers as highly unlikely, due to the overcapacities in the European banking sector," he said. -- Zurich Editorial, +41 1 631 7340
